findings.reason: the release leg already reads the export report's candidate/published/exclusion values, the two forms agree, and the plan's design does not rest on where the residue is computed, so extending export.py to publish the residue and having catalog_release.py read it is a cleanup the plan need not carry.
findings.text: _record_* accounting recomputes accounting_residue = candidate_count − published_count − len(exclusions) that the export report already computes and serializes at export.py:480, so the same arithmetic has two implementations and a change to one can silently disagree with the other

findings.reason: the sections must account for the added refusal surface in their own text (name the retired/merged family, or state why the new refusal cannot fold into the existing gate refusal), which changes how the nodes are written.
findings.text: the sections that add refusal surface (the §2a import refusal and the §3 exclusion-accounting refusal) state that they extend existing gates but do not name, in their own text, any refusal family they retire or merge, against a supplied refusal_families figure of 0

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the exclusion ledger hides the whole accounting in one gate and one record type: _run_exclusion_accounting_gate (export.py:1313) sits behind the existing GateResult bundle, and ExclusionRecord/report (export.py:299, :375) carries per-reason identities and the emitted+exclusions=N arithmetic. The interface added is one gate and one record shape, not a spread of counters.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the release rehearsal re-derives the accounting residue that the export report already serializes, so one arithmetic has two owners.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2a ("refused rather than logged") and §3 ("a refusal, not a warning") each add a refusal path and the section text names no refusal path it retires or merges.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every mechanism the plan proposes names and extends an on-disk owner rather than rebuilding it: the exclusion ledger extends the existing gates A/B/C in imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:1313 and _fetch_candidates (export.py:512); the import guard extends protection.PROTECTED_FIELDS (protection.py:26); the structural authority record reuses graph_ops._persist_structural_authority (parents.py:507); the age-aware claim preflight sources defaults.DEFAULT_ORPHAN_SWEEP_TIMEOUT_S (defaults.py:64); the per-pool abandon extends the existing stall watchdog in pools.py. No subsystem is added without a cited search.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no thin forwarding layer over existing machinery. Its import change turns the ad-hoc catalog import into a proposal routed through the existing sn edit review path (edit.py), and the §4 lineage decision retires behaviour rather than wrapping it: _fetch_deprecation_stubs (export.py:1695) now returns [] (supersession lineage is graph-internal), so an emitted surface was removed, not added.
